data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's OOD-probe requirement is in tension with the problem's constraint of 'a single evaluation.' The target asserts that 'without out-of-distribution probe items, checklist compliance and genuine cue extraction are observationally equivalent,' and demands held-out cases the checklist was not designed for. But within a single evaluation, the OOD probe design itself requires knowledge of the checklist's design distribution to define what counts as OOD—an external standard not available from within the evaluation alone. Moreover, the target's own countercondition acknowledges the problem: if the expert's intuition also fails on OOD probes (both are in-distribution estimators), the divergence is uninformative. This means the OOD diagnostic only works under the narrow condition where the expert generalizes but the panel does not, which presupposes the very thing the evaluation is meant to establish (that the expert has genuine understanding the checklist lacks). The target thus smuggles in a prior about expert generalization capacity that a single evaluation cannot provide, making the diagnostic circular for the claim it is meant to support.
